title: FastHandshake + Typed Resume: patterns for low-latency tool-calling and progressive structured output (wip)
summary: Working draft proposing a compact handshake and typed-resume approach for hosted streaming API calls that combine low-latency token streaming, explicit tool-call handoffs, and resumable client behavior. Aim: make incremental structured outputs reliable for mobile/edge clients and short OLTP interactions while preserving server-side routing/backoff semantics.
goals: Design a compact, backwards-compatible streaming handshake that lets clients and SDKs opt into typed frames (events, tool-call intents, structured outputs) without expensive negotiation round trips.
Define a typed-resume token format and resume semantics so interrupted sessions (mobile flakiness, token limits) can be resumed with strong ordering guarantees and partial-KV cache reuse.
Propose SDK ergonomics for client-side host exposures: retry semantics, default fallbacks for partial structured frames, and idiomatic helper methods for tool invocation and replay.
Specify telemetry fields and SLOs needed to detect degradation of structured-tool handoffs and resume failures (observability-first).
non_goals: Full security and encryption spec (we'll reference existing KMS/HSM guidelines in private deployments).
Replacing existing long-poll sync endpoints — this focuses on streaming-first scenarios.
Formal protocol standardization across third-party runtimes — initial iteration for Redwood Hosted API only.
context_and_motivations: Customers increasingly use hosted streaming for short interactive operations: auto-summarization, stepwise SQL generation, and conversational tool orchestration. Current patterns have two pain points: 1) heuristic parsing of partial text frames complicates tool-call detection and increases client errors; 2) mobile/edge clients often drop connections and cannot efficiently resume in a way that reuses server-side KV caches or batching state. We need a compact handshake and typed frame system for incremental outputs that makes tool intent explicit, provides replayable resume tokens, and is easy to adopt in SDKs.
constraints: Must work over existing HTTP/2 streaming and WebSocket gateways — no new transport required.
Negotiation must be single round: client indicates feature flags in initial request headers/body, server responds in first frame with confirmed capabilities and resume token policy.
Server-side rollout must be incremental: feature flag off by default, opt-in via model-route config or per-client header.
Keep additional latency per-token negligible (target <= 0.5ms added per token in p99 cases).
user_stories: As an app developer, I want my mobile client to start an assistant session, allow the model to call an external 'search' tool mid-stream, and resume the stream after a temporary network disconnect without re-generating prior tokens.

As an SDK user, I want a typed event API that surfaces 'tool-intent' and 'tool-result' frames so my client can render a UI affordance (e.g., show 'calling calendar API') instead of guessing from raw text.
As an SRE, I want telemetry that lets me correlate resume failures with KV cache misses so we can find regressions when kernel selection or quantization changes cause resume incompatibility.
proposed_handshake: High level: client includes header X-RW-Streaming-Features: typed_frames,resume_v1 in the initial POST (or WS open). Server replies with the first streaming frame — a Type="capabilities" frame — confirming accepted features and returning a short resume policy id and server-side session id. The rest of the stream uses compact typed frames (small binary-ish JSON lines) with an explicit `frame_type` field: 'tokens', 'event', 'tool_call', 'tool_result', 'checkpoint', 'end'. Checkpoints emit resume tokens. Frame shapes are stable and documented in api_contract_examples. (Implementation note: we encode frames as newline-delimited JSON to remain human readable for logs while being compact.)
typed_frame_primitives: tokens: (partial text tokens) — same as current streaming tokens but wrapped: {frame_type: 'tokens', token_delta: '...'}.
tool_call: declarative tool intent — {frame_type: 'tool_call', tool: 'search', args_schema: 'json-schema-ref', intent_id: 'uuid'}
tool_result: the tool output binding — {frame_type: 'tool_result', intent_id: 'uuid', payload: '...'}.
checkpoint: server-generated resume anchor — {frame_type: 'checkpoint', resume_token: 'base64v1', seq: 1234}.
resume_semantics: Resume tokens are opaque base64v1 strings that encode: session_id, last_applied_seq, server_kv_epoch, and an HMAC. Clients can present a resume token in a followup request header X-RW-Resume-Token. Server validates token metadata; if server_kv_epoch matches current model runtime epoch, the server will attempt to reuse cached KV & batch state from last_applied_seq and continue generation with deterministic ordering guarantees. If epoch mismatch occurs, server returns a special first-frame 'resume_rejected' with reason 'kv_epoch_mismatch' and a suggested re-run policy (either full restart or fast-replay). Resume attempts count toward per-request rate limits. Resume tokens are short-lived (default TTL 5 minutes) and configurable per-route.
client_and_sdk_guidance: SDKs should expose a high-level `startStream({features: [...]})` that returns a typed-frame async iterator to consumers.

Provide `on('tool_call', handler)` and `on('tool_result', handler)` shorthands. Handlers receive typed payloads and a convenience `ack()` method that sends a small ack frame so servers may prioritize tooling latency.

Retries: client should attempt local reconnects immediately (exponential backoff capped at 3 attempts) and include the last checkpoint resume_token. If resume is rejected, SDK falls back to a transparent restart with a `partial_replay` flag (if developer opts-in) that provides best-effort merging of previously emitted structured frames.

Mobile guidance: keep checkpointing cadence aggressive for flaky networks (default checkpoint every 1-2s or 32 tokens), but provide server controls for checkpoint budget per-request to avoid high state churn.
api_contract_examples: Example handshake request: POST /v1/responses?model=redwood-stream-1 with header X-RW-Streaming-Features: typed_frames,resume_v1. Initial server capability frame: {"frame_type": "capabilities", "features": ["typed_frames", "resume_v1"], "resume_policy": {"ttl_s": 300, "checkpoint_every_ms": 2000}}. Example stream sequence: capabilities -> tokens -> tokens -> tool_call(intent_id=abc) -> checkpoint(resume_token=xxx) -> tool_result(intent_id=abc) -> tokens -> end.
sdk_ergonomics_examples: JavaScript: const it = client.startStream({features: ['typed_frames', 'resume_v1']}); for await (const frame of it) { if(frame.frame_type==='tool_call') await client.callTool(frame); }
Python: stream = client.responses.stream(...); stream.on('tool_call', lambda f: handle_tool(f)); resume is available as stream.last_checkpoint
observability_and_slos: Add structured telemetry events: handshake.latency, checkpoint.emit.latency, resume.attempt, resume.success, resume.reject.reason, toolcall.latency, toolresult.latency. Build dashboards that break down resume_reject reasons by kv_epoch and by model variant. SLOs: resume_success_rate >= 99.0% on stable routes; avg handshake.latency < 50ms global p95; checkpoint_emit_latency p95 < 100ms.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (behind ff): implement server-side parser and capability frame, no SDK changes. Internal teams opt-in by route config.
Phase 1 (SDK beta): expose JS/Python opt-in helpers; gate by client header. Run internal Canary with Solutions Engineering customers.
Phase 2 (Wider bake): flip route-level default to 'enabled for devs' and monitor resume_success metrics; add mobile sample app.
Phase 3 (GA): enable documented defaults, add additional language SDKs and orchestration support for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Kill switch: ability to disable typed_frames/resume_v1 per-region quickly.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end demo of a mobile app that starts a session, experiences an intermittent disconnect, resumes with a resume token, and receives the expected tool_result and tokens in-order.
Telemetry shows resume_success_rate >= 99% across 1 week in canary orgs, with no meaningful p99 latency regression on token emission.
SDKs provide ergonomic helpers and docs with code samples and migration notes for clients that previously parsed raw text for tool intents.
security_and_privacy_notes: Resume tokens contain HMAC and are short-lived; they should not be persisted beyond TTL. For private deployments, route-level policy must be available to set resume TTL to 0 (disable). Tool_call payloads may include PII — recommend server-side redact hooks and explicit config to block checkpointing sensitive payloads.
open_questions: Should resume tokens be refreshable (sliding window) if client remains active? safety vs state-bloat tradeoff.
What's the optimal default checkpoint cadence for low-latency workloads vs state storage costs? (1s vs 32 tokens vs size-based checkpointing).
How to version resume token encoding to allow graceful kernel-level changes without invalidating all tokens? (we propose `base64v1` with a small header).
Should tool_result payloads support streaming chunking (large binary blobs) or only small JSON payloads?
next_steps_and_todo: 1) Engineering spike to implement minimal capability frame + typed frame parser. 2) SDK PoC for JS + Python with async iterator support. 3) Build telemetry events and dashboard. 4) Draft migration guide for teams using heuristic tool parsing. Assign owners and add tickets (ENG-1348, SDK-298).
notes: This is intentionally compact and pragmatic — we prioritize small behavioral changes to make client implementations easier without an entire protocol rewrite. Expect follow-ups to iterate on resume token lifecycle and explicit tool security policies.
